title: Redwood + CloudBridge Joint Solution & Marketplace Listing - Tech Sync
next_steps: Redwood SE to draft reference architecture doc and share by 2027-01-05
CloudBridge to provide marketplace listing assets (logos, copy, pricing) by 2026-12-29
Schedule joint solution review with legal for marketplace terms week of 2027-01-09
Run integration smoke tests in staging; Redwood to supply test plan by 2026-12-27
action_items: Sophie Patel - Draft reference architecture diagram and infra checklist - due 2027-01-05
Priya Singh - Share marketplace marketing assets and preferred listing description - due 2026-12-29
Anil Kapoor - Provide sample terraform snippets and RBAC guide - due 2026-12-30
Lina Park - Send SCOP2/ISO scope questions and encryption requirements - due 2026-12-28
Evan Brooks - Coordinate legal review and share draft MSA with CloudBridge - due 2027-01-10
summary: Technical sync to align on joint solution architecture for Redwood + CloudBridge marketplace listing. Discussed reference architecture, security controls (KMS/SSO/audit logs), marketplace assets and approval flow, integration touchpoints (VPC peering, onboarding, billing), and next steps for docs and smoke tests.
questions: Do we need a separate VPC option for the marketplace listing?
What level of logging/audit will be surfaced to CloudBridge customers?
Is SAML SSO required for initial pilots or post-GA?
transcript:
[00:00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Evan from Redwood — we got Sophie and Anil on the line too. How's everyone?
[00:00:08] Priya: Hey Evan, Priya here. Thanks, good. Busy week but excited to get this moving.
[00:00:12] Marco: Marco — quick note, gonna chime in on the DevRel angles.
[00:00:18] Sophie: Cool. Goal for today — align on the architecture we ship in the marketplace listing and what pieces need reference docs, plus a run-book for onboarding.
[00:00:28] Priya: Perfect. Also want to confirm the approval path on our side — marketing + legal — and any dependencies.
[00:00:34] Anil: Quick caveat up front: some of our infra suggestions assume a VPC peering or private link; if CloudBridge prefers shared hosted endpoints, we can propose an alternative.
[00:00:44] Lina: For security, we need to confirm KMS integration and bring-your-own-key options, plus audit logs retention.
[00:00:50] Evan: Totally — those are top of mind for enterprise partners. Sophie, can you walk through the reference arch?
[00:00:56] Sophie: Yep. So picture this: customer route — marketplace listing triggers provisioning on their account, which then either spins up a Redwood-managed endpoint in their VPC via private deployment or points to our hosted endpoint with a dedicated tenancy. We'll show two patterns in the doc: "Hosted—dedicated" and "Private—VPC".
[00:01:18] Marco: Could you repeat the dedicated tenancy bit — are we talking dedicated capacity or just isolated project?
[00:01:24] Sophie: Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools we can map per tenant, so predictable throughput. For marketplace, listing will indicate an option for reserved capacity add-on.
[00:01:34] Priya: For CloudBridge customers, many will want the private VPC option. Do you have a reference flow for peering?
[00:01:40] Anil: Yes — typical is VPC peering or PrivateLink; we'll provide terraform snippets and an RBAC guide for the service account that Redwood creates. There may be small ip range requirements.
[00:01:52] Lina: On encryption, BYOK important — we need to know if Redwood supports external KMS and HSM options, and whether keys can be rotated without downtime.
[00:02:02] Sophie: We support KMS integrations; HSM via customer-managed KMS is on the roadmap — we'll put a clear note. Key rotation should be seamless for data at rest; we'll confirm specifics and add to the security FAQ.
[00:02:15] Priya: Audit logs? retention windows? Some customers require 12+ months.
[00:02:20] Anil: Our observability stack can export audit logs to partner buckets — retention is configurable. We'll include a recommended pipeline in the reference arch.
[00:02:29] Priya: Great. Next, marketplace listing — what assets do you need from CloudBridge?
[00:02:34] Evan: Typically logos, short (50-100 word) blurb, longer product description, screenshots, and a pricing/packaging matrix. Also any joint case studies if available.
[00:02:45] Marco: We can get marketing assets by end of next week; I'll own that.
[00:02:50] Priya: I'll coordinate legal review, expect turnaround maybe 1–2 weeks depending on holidays.
[00:02:56] Sophie: For the listing, we want to show a clear reference architecture diagram — we'll draft one with two variants. Also include an onboarding checklist: account mapping, auth setup (SAML), network reqs, test plan.
[00:03:12] Marco: On SAML, is that required for GA? We have customers that want SSO but some pilots don't need it.
[00:03:18] Anil: Recommend SAML for enterprise GA; for pilot we can support API keys and invite flows. We'll note both.
[00:03:26] Lina: And what about data residency? Some customers want EU-only.
[00:03:30] Sophie: We'll surface region controls and the option to pin deployments to specific regions. We'll document latency profiles per region in the listing.
[00:03:40] Priya: Billing flow — who bills the end customer, CloudBridge or Redwood?
[00:03:44] Evan: Marketplace model can be flexible. Two options: CloudBridge resells and bills, or Redwood bills with revenue share. We should get both legal teams to sign off. Evan: we'll put the recommended default as CloudBridge billing for bundled offerings.
[00:03:58] Marco: OK makes sense. For joint solutions we might want a single checkout experience — any caveats?
[00:04:03] Anil: Need clear entitlement mapping and an integration in the provisioning API; we'll supply an example webhook and terraform module.
[00:04:12] [00:04:45] Sophie: Quick note — there's a small transcription glitch in the last demo with KV cache mention, sometimes shows "KV cache" as "K V cash" in older transcripts, so ignore that.
[00:04:58] Marco: ha, noted.
[00:05:02] Priya: Can we run a smoke test in staging? Our platform team can open a sandbox account.
[00:05:07] Sophie: Absolutely. Redwood will supply a test plan and a small benchmark harness. We'll aim to have the test plan by 2026-12-27.
[00:05:16] Priya: That timeline should work. Also customers might ask about model version pinning — how granular is model version control?
[00:05:24] Anil: Customers can pin model versions per-route; we also support rollouts and can fallback to compatible model variants automatically. We'll document recommended configs for POC vs prod.
[00:05:37] Priya: Anything we need on network egress or IP allowlist?
[00:05:40] Anil: We'll supply a range of egress IPs and minimal ports — standard HTTPS plus optional port for private links.
[00:05:49] Marco: Security review — Lina will send a short list of SOC2/ISO questions.
[00:05:53] Lina: Yes I'll compile and send by Monday.
[00:05:56] Evan: Great. On timeline: if assets come in by 12/29 and reference arch by 01/05, we can aim for staged listing by mid-Jan and a pilot the following week. Legal review could be the gating factor.
[00:06:09] Priya: Sounds realistic.
[00:06:12] Sophie: For the reference arch doc we'll include: architecture diagram, terraform snippets, RBAC example, KMS notes, audit log flow, onboarding checklist, FAQ.
[00:06:25] Marco: For DevRel we'd love a "quickstart" repo — simple deploy script for a demo app.
[00:06:30] Anil: We'll open-source a demo repo and link it in the listing.
[00:06:34] Priya: Anything else on GA features vs pilot?
[00:06:38] Sophie: Pilot: hosted endpoint + optional dedicated capacity, API keys or invite SSO. GA: SAML, BYOK, regional pinning, longer retention.
[00:06:48] Priya: Good.
[00:06:50] Evan: Alright let's recap actions — Sophie to draft arch and test plan, Anil terraform snippets, Priya marketing assets and legal review, Lina security questions, Evan coordinate MSA. We'll set follow-up for two weeks out.
[00:07:05] Marco: Thanks everyone.
[00:07:07] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:07:10] Evan: Thanks all — we'll send notes and next steps.
[00:07:15] [END]
